What will come in the place of the question mark ‘(?)’ in the following equation, if ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged and ‘−’ and ‘+’ are interchanged?

72 − 5 + 42 ÷ 7 × 1 = ?

Now, we solve the equation following the BODMAS rule:

= 72 − 5 + __**42 ÷ 7**__ × 1

= 72 − 5 + __**6 × 1**__

= __**72 − 5**__ + 6

= __**67 + 6**__

= 73

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question: As per Sample Registration System (SRS) Bulletin 2020, what was the difference between death rates of rural and urban India?
questions.solution:

• The Sample Registration System (SRS) Bulletin 2020 revealed that the death rate in rural India was higher compared to urban India.
 
• The rural death rate was recorded at 6.9 per 1,000 population, while the urban death rate was 5.6 per 1,000 population.
 
• The difference between the death rates of rural and urban areas stood at 1.3 as per the SRS Bulletin 2020.
 
• Death rates are influenced by factors such as healthcare access, lifestyle, and socio-economic conditions.
 
• This data highlights disparities in health infrastructure and living conditions between rural and urban regions in India.

• SRS is a demographic survey conducted in India to provide reliable annual estimates of birth rate, death rate, and other vital statistics.
 
• It functions under the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Death Rates:**
 
 
• Access to healthcare facilities, nutrition, sanitation, and socio-economic conditions play a crucial role in determining death rates.
 
• Rural areas often face challenges such as poor healthcare infrastructure and limited access to emergency services.
 
 
 
• **Urban vs. Rural Health Disparities:**
 
 
• Urban areas typically have better access to healthcare facilities, emergency services, and sanitation.
 
• Rural regions may lack adequate medical facilities, leading to higher mortality rates.
 
 
 
• **Policy Interventions:**
 
 
• Government schemes like Ayushman Bharat aim to bridge the gap in healthcare access between rural and urban areas.
 
• Improving rural health infrastructure is a key focus area for reducing disparities in death rates.

• The **Indian Association** was founded in 1876 by **Surendranath Banerjee** and **Anandamohan Bose** in Calcutta (now Kolkata).
 
• The Indian Association was established with the primary objective of creating a strong public opinion against British policies and promoting political unity among Indians.
 
• It aimed to build a platform for educated Indians to demand reforms in British governance and represent Indian issues to the colonial rulers.
 
• The Indian Association played a vital role in organizing the first-ever **Indian National Conference in 1883**, which served as a precursor to the Indian National Congress.
 
• It was one of the earliest organizations that worked towards creating political awareness and fostering unity among Indians during the pre-Congress era.

• He was one of the earliest leaders of India's nationalist movement and is often referred to as the "father of Indian nationalism."
 
• He founded the newspaper **“The Bengalee”** to spread awareness and mobilize public opinion against colonial policies.
 
• Surendranath Banerjee was a key figure in the Indian National Congress and advocated for constitutional reforms and self-rule.
 
 
 
• **Anandamohan Bose:**
 
 
• He was a prominent social reformer, nationalist, and one of the founding members of the Indian Association.
 
• Anandamohan Bose was the first Indian to graduate from the University of Cambridge with honors in mathematics.
 
• He worked actively for the upliftment of society and contributed significantly to the Indian nationalist movement.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Conference:**
 
 
• The Indian National Conference was organized in 1883 and 1885 by the Indian Association to discuss political and social reforms.
 
• It was a precursor to the Indian National Congress and inspired the formation of the Congress in 1885.
 
 
 
• **Pre-Congress Political Organizations:**
 
 
• Before the Indian National Congress, political organizations like the Indian Association, Bombay Presidency Association, and Poona Sarvajanik Sabha laid the foundation of the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• These organizations focused on creating political awareness and mobilizing educated Indians for reforms and self-governance.

questions.question: Which dynasty succeeded the Mauryan Empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shunga Dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Shunga Dynasty was established by **Pushyamitra Shunga**, who overthrew the Mauryan emperor Brihadratha in 185 BCE.
 
• Pushyamitra Shunga was originally a **commander-in-chief** in the Mauryan army.
 
• The Shunga Dynasty ruled over parts of northern and central India, with its capital at **Pataliputra**.
 
• The reign of the Shunga Dynasty is marked by the revival of **Brahmanical traditions** and the decline of Buddhism.
 
• The Shunga rulers were patrons of art and architecture, contributing significantly to the construction of **stupas and temples**, including enhancements to the Bharhut and Sanchi stupas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pushyamitra Shunga:**

 
 
• He was the founder of the Shunga Dynasty and ruled from 185 BCE to 149 BCE.
 
• He is known for conducting **Vedic sacrifices** such as the Ashvamedha Yajna (horse sacrifice).
 
 
 
• **Decline of Buddhism:**
 
 
• The Shunga period saw a decline in royal patronage for Buddhism, although common people continued to practice it.
 
• The dynasty supported **Brahmanical Hinduism**, leading to a cultural shift.
 
 
 
• **Art and Architecture:**
 
 
• The Shunga rulers are known for their contributions to Indian art, particularly in the form of stupas like Bharhut and Sanchi.
 
• The period also witnessed the development of early Hindu temple architecture.
 
 
 
• **Kanva Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Kanva Dynasty succeeded the Shunga Dynasty after its decline around 73 BCE.
 
• The Kanva rulers were Brahmanical and continued the cultural legacy initiated by the Shungas.

questions.question: The concept of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India is inspired by which country's constitution?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties were incorporated into the Indian Constitution via the **42nd Amendment Act** in 1976.
 
• This concept was inspired by the Constitution of the former **Soviet Union**, which emphasized the duties of citizens alongside their rights.
 
• Initially, 10 Fundamental Duties were included; an additional duty was added later through the **86th Amendment Act** in 2002.
 
• Fundamental Duties are listed under **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution and serve as moral obligations for citizens.
 
• The aim is to promote a sense of responsibility and national unity among Indian citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Amendment Act (1976):**

 
 
• Known as the "Mini Constitution," it introduced several significant changes, including Fundamental Duties, the Preamble, and changes to the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added based on the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A:**
 
 
• It lists 11 Fundamental Duties, such as respecting the Constitution, promoting harmony, and protecting the environment.
 
 
 
• **86th Amendment Act (2002):**
 
 
• This amendment added the duty of providing opportunities for education to children between the ages of 6 to 14 years.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• While many constitutions focus predominantly on rights, the Soviet Union emphasized both rights and duties to ensure collective responsibility.
 
• India adopted a similar approach to align with its socio-cultural ethos and promote civic responsibility.

questions.question: What is one significant drawback of the Green Revolution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Loss of biodiversity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution, which began in the mid-20th century, significantly increased agricultural productivity but led to the **loss of biodiversity** as it focused on monoculture farming.
 
• High-yielding varieties (HYVs) of crops like wheat and rice were heavily promoted, replacing traditional crop varieties and reducing **genetic diversity**.
 
• The extensive use of chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and herbicides further degraded ecosystems, harming **pollinators, insects, and soil microorganisms**.
 
• The reliance on a few crop species made agricultural systems more vulnerable to **diseases, pests, and climate change**, as genetic diversity acts as a natural buffer.
 
• Regions with rich agricultural traditions saw the **disappearance of indigenous crop varieties**, which were often better suited to local conditions and required fewer inputs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monoculture:** The practice of growing a single crop over a large area, which increases productivity but reduces biodiversity and makes crops more susceptible to pests and diseases.
 
• **High-Yielding Varieties (HYVs):** These are genetically improved crop varieties that produce more output per hectare but require significant inputs like water, fertilizers, and pesticides.
 
• **Agrochemical Dependency:** The Green Revolution led to the intensive use of synthetic fertilizers and pesticides, which caused soil degradation and water contamination.
 
• **Soil Health and Fertility:** Continuous monoculture and excessive chemical use diminished soil organic matter, leading to decreased fertility over time.
 
• **Sustainable Agriculture:** Practices like crop rotation, organic farming, and the use of traditional seeds are being promoted to counteract the negative impacts of the Green Revolution and restore biodiversity.

questions.question: In a state, the Council of Ministers are collectively responsible to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State Legislative Assembly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Council of Ministers in a state is **collectively responsible to the State Legislative Assembly** as per Article 164 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This collective responsibility implies that the entire council works as a unit and stands or falls together in the assembly.
 
• If the State Legislative Assembly passes a vote of no-confidence against the council, all its members including the Chief Minister must resign.
 
• The Chief Minister serves as the leader of the Council of Ministers and communicates the collective decisions of the council to the Governor.
 
• The principle of collective responsibility ensures accountability of the executive (Council of Ministers) to the legislative body (State Assembly).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor's Role**: The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and appoints the Chief Minister and other ministers on the CM’s advice. However, the council is not collectively responsible to the Governor.
 
• **Article 164**: This article lays down the provision of the council's collective responsibility to the legislative assembly and provides the constitutional framework for the functioning of the state government.
 
• **Vote of No-Confidence**: It is a parliamentary motion moved in the legislative assembly to demonstrate that the council no longer has the majority support of the house.
 
• **Individual vs. Collective Responsibility**: While individual ministers are responsible for their respective portfolios, collective responsibility ensures that the council acts unanimously and stands together on all decisions.
 
• **Constitutional Comparison**: This principle of collective responsibility is similar to the responsibility of the Union Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha at the central level.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement of the following.

options.text: Vitamin C facilitates absorption and utilisation of iron in the body.
Vitamin C plays an important role in collagen synthesis.
Vitamin A, E and C act as antioxidants.
Fat is considered as a good source of energy during the exercise and competition.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fat is considered as a good source of energy during the exercise and competition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fat is not considered a primary source of energy during exercise and competition; carbohydrates are preferred due to their quicker energy release.
 
• During high-intensity exercise, the body primarily relies on glycogen stored in muscles and liver for energy.
 
• Fat metabolism requires more oxygen and takes longer, making it less efficient as a source of immediate energy during exercise.
 
• Fat is utilized as a significant energy source during prolonged, low-intensity activities when carbohydrate reserves are depleted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Role of Vitamin C:** Vitamin C enhances iron absorption by reducing ferric iron (Fe3+) to ferrous iron (Fe2+), which is more readily absorbed in the intestines.
 
• **Collagen Synthesis:** Vitamin C is essential in the hydroxylation of proline and lysine, which are critical steps in collagen formation.
 
• **Antioxidant Properties:** Vitamins A, E, and C act as antioxidants, neutralizing free radicals and protecting cells from oxidative damage.
 
• **Energy Sources During Exercise:** Carbohydrates are the main energy source for high-intensity exercise, while fats are utilized during prolonged, moderate-intensity activities.
 
• **Metabolic Differences:** Carbohydrate metabolism is anaerobic and faster, while fat metabolism is aerobic and slower but provides sustained energy for long-duration activities.

• The ECI has the responsibility to ensure the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) is followed during elections.
 
• Under Article 324 of the Indian Constitution, the ECI has the authority to supervise, direct, and control the entire election process.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**
 
 
• Article 324: Provides for the establishment of the Election Commission.
 
• Article 325: Prohibits discrimination in the preparation of electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste, or sex.
 
• Article 326: Grants universal adult suffrage, allowing all citizens of 18 years and above to vote.
 
 
 
• **Chief Election Commissioner (CEC):**

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a progressive tax system?

options.text: Tax rate increases as the taxable amount increases
Uniform tax rate for all income groups
Tax rate decreases as the taxable amount increases
Higher tax rate for corporations than individuals

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tax rate increases as the taxable amount increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A progressive tax system is one where the tax rate increases as the taxable income or amount increases.
 
• This system is designed to impose a higher tax burden on individuals or entities with higher incomes, ensuring equitable distribution of wealth.
 
• It is commonly used in many countries to reduce income inequality and provide funds for public services.
 
• Examples of progressive taxes include income tax brackets, where higher income levels are taxed at higher rates.
 
• The principle of "ability to pay" is central to progressive taxation, meaning those with greater financial resources contribute more.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regressive Tax:** A tax system where the tax rate decreases as the taxable amount increases, disproportionately affecting lower-income earners.
 
• **Proportional Tax:** Also known as a flat tax, it applies the same tax rate to all income levels, regardless of the amount earned.
 
• **Examples of Progressive Tax:** U.S. Federal Income Tax, where tax brackets increase with higher income levels.
 
• **Tax Brackets:** Income ranges defined by law where specific tax rates apply, forming the foundation of progressive taxation.
 
• **Redistribution of Wealth:** Progressive taxation aims to reduce economic disparities by transferring resources from higher-income earners to fund programs for the broader population.

questions.question: Which of the following can be separated from a mixture by the process of centrifugation, but NOT by the process of filtration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Colloid only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **colloid** is a heterogeneous mixture where fine particles are dispersed in a medium but do not settle down due to their small size.
 
• Filtration cannot separate colloidal particles as their size (1-1000 nm) is smaller than the pores of a filter paper.
 
• **Centrifugation** is an effective method for separating colloidal particles by spinning the mixture at high speed, causing the denser colloidal particles to sediment.
 
• Suspensions, in contrast, can be separated by both filtration and centrifugation due to their larger particle size.
 
• Solutions cannot be separated by either filtration or centrifugation, as the solute particles are dissolved at the molecular level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Colloid:** A mixture where the dispersed particles do not settle or separate on standing. Examples include milk, fog, and jelly.
 
• **Suspension:** A heterogeneous mixture with larger particles (greater than 1000 nm) that settle over time. Examples include muddy water and sand in water.
 
• **Solution:** A homogeneous mixture where solute particles are completely dissolved and cannot be separated by any physical methods like filtration or centrifugation. Examples include saltwater and sugar dissolved in water.
 
• **Centrifugation:** A process of separating components of a mixture based on their densities by spinning it at high speed. It is commonly used in laboratories and industries.
 
• **Filtration:** A mechanical or physical process to separate solids from liquids or gases using a medium that allows only certain particles to pass through (e.g., filter paper).

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper promises to sell his goods at cost price. However, he uses a weight that actually weighs 32% less than what is written on it. Find his profit percentage.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the claimed weight be 100 units.

Since the goods are sold at cost price, Selling Price (SP) = 100 units.

Actual weight given to the customer = 100 − 32 = 68 units.

Cost Price (CP) for the shopkeeper = 68 units.

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100 = (32 ÷ 68) × 100 = 800 ÷ 17 = 47 ¹/₁₇ %.

**∴ The correct answer is 47 ¹/₁₇ %.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The shopkeeper promises to sell his goods at cost price.

He uses a weight that is 32% less than the marked weight.

**Formula Used:**

Profit % = (Claimed Weight − Actual Weight) ÷ Actual Weight × 100

 
 Claimed Weight = 100 units (SP)
 
 
 Actual Weight = 68 units (CP)
 
 
 Profit = 32
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 Profit % = (32 ÷ 68) × 100 ≈ 47.05%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the true marked weight be 1000 g.

⇒ False actual weight = 1000 − (32% of 1000) = 1000 − 320 = 680 g.

⇒ Since he sells at CP, he charges for 1000 g but gives only 680 g.

⇒ Cost Price (CP) for the shopkeeper = Cost of 680 g.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) for the shopkeeper = Cost of 1000 g.

⇒ Profit made = 1000 − 680 = 320 g equivalent.

⇒ Profit % = (320 ÷ 680) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (8 ÷ 17) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 800 ÷ 17 = 47 ¹/₁₇ %

**∴ The correct answer is 47 ¹/₁₇ %.**

Dishonest Dealer (Selling at CP)

When a shopkeeper sells goods at cost price but uses a false weight, his Profit % is calculated directly as (Error ÷ True Weight Given) × 100.

Dishonest Dealer (Selling at Profit/Loss)

If the dealer marks up the price and also cheats on weight, the overall ratio is SP ÷ CP = (Claimed Weight ÷ Actual Weight) × (Price Charged ÷ Actual Price).

Successive Changes

To calculate the net effect of two successive percentage changes A% and B%, use the net change formula: A + B + (A × B) ÷ 100.

questions.question: The smallest natural number which is divisible by 12, 28, 36 and 27 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the smallest number divisible by 12, 28, 36, and 27, calculate their LCM.

Since 36 is a multiple of 12, we can omit 12 and directly find the LCM of 28, 36, and 27.

LCM of 36 (4 × 9) and 27 (3 × 9) is 108.

Now, LCM of 108 and 28 (which is 4 × 7) is 108 × 7 = 756.

**∴ The correct answer is 756.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 12, 28, 36, and 27.

**Method Used:**

The smallest natural number completely divisible by a given set of numbers is their Lowest Common Multiple (LCM).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 28 = 2² × 7

⇒ Prime factorization of 36 = 2² × 3²

⇒ Prime factorization of 27 = 3³

⇒ The prime factors present in all given numbers are 2, 3, and 7.

⇒ The highest power of 2 is 2² = 4

⇒ The highest power of 3 is 3³ = 27

⇒ The highest power of 7 is 7¹ = 7

⇒ LCM = Product of the highest powers of all prime factors

⇒ LCM = 4 × 27 × 7

⇒ LCM = 108 × 7

⇒ LCM = 756

**∴ The correct answer is 756.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Lowest Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest non-zero number that is a multiple of all the given numbers. It is found by multiplying the highest powers of all prime factors.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The greatest number that divides all the given numbers completely. It is found by multiplying the lowest powers of common prime factors.

Product Rule of LCM and HCF

For any two positive integers a and b: a × b = LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b). This rule strictly applies to pairs of numbers only.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are called co-prime if their HCF is 1. The LCM of two co-prime numbers is simply their direct product.
</p
